summary: Neural network architecture using self-attention mechanisms, foundational to modern LLMs since 2017

content.overview: The Transformer is the foundational neural network architecture for modern LLMs, introduced in the 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need' (173,000+ citations, top 10 most-cited papers of 21st century). Unlike previous architectures using recurrence or convolution, Transformers rely entirely on self-attention mechanisms to process sequences. The CRITICAL limitation: Self-attention has quadratic computational complexity O(n²) with sequence length, making long contexts exponentially expensive. This quadratic cost is the root cause of context window limits and why 200K token requests cost ~4x more than 100K token requests.
keyPoints: Self-attention mechanism: Each token attends to ALL other tokens in the sequence to compute its representation - this enables parallel processing (unlike RNNs)
CRITICAL LIMITATION: Attention complexity is O(n²) where n = sequence length - doubling context length quadruples computation cost
Multi-head attention: Run multiple attention 'heads' in parallel (e.g., 32 heads), each learning different patterns (syntax, semantics, long-range dependencies)
Query-Key-Value (QKV) paradigm: Each token generates Query (what I'm looking for), Key (what I offer), Value (what I contain) vectors; attention = softmax(Q·K)·V
Modern optimizations (2025): FlashAttention v2 improves throughput by ~32% (145k → 192k tokens/sec), attention approximation reduces quadratic cost
Transformers are STATELESS - no built-in memory across requests; context window is the only 'memory' available
Encoder-decoder vs. decoder-only: LLMs (GPT, Claude) use decoder-only; translation models (T5) use encoder-decoder
warnings: Quadratic cost makes extremely long contexts (1M+ tokens) prohibitively expensive and slow - even with optimizations
Attention does NOT guarantee understanding - models can attend to tokens without comprehending meaning (pattern matching vs. reasoning)
Position encodings are critical - without them, transformers can't distinguish token order ('cat ate fish' vs. 'fish ate cat')
Self-attention can create attention sinks - models over-attend to specific tokens (often first token) regardless of relevance
Training transformers requires massive compute - GPT-4 scale models need thousands of GPUs for months, inaccessible to most organizations
Transformers struggle with tasks requiring precise counting, arithmetic, or long-range exact recall - architecture limitations
